                    ### Question
                    A 5-year-old boy is brought to the physician because of a painful, burning rash on his left arm for 3 days. Three years ago, he was diagnosed with heart failure due to congenital heart disease and received an allogeneic heart transplantation. He takes cyclosporine to prevent chronic transplant rejection. He has not received any routine childhood vaccinations. A photograph of the rash is shown. Microscopic examination of a skin biopsy specimen is most likely to show which of the following findings?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Eosinophilic spongiosis and subepidermal blister formation
opb. Multinucleated epidermal giant cells and intranuclear inclusions
opc. Papillary microabscesses and granular deposits of IgA
opd. Fungal hyphae and hyperkeratosis
ope. Gram-positive cocci and spongiotic dermatitis

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The skin biopsy of the rash on the boy's left arm, given his history of heart transplantation and cyclosporine use, is most likely to show findings related to increased risk of infections. This could include features such as fungal hyphae, indicating a possible fungal infection, rather than other options like eosinophilic spongiosis or intranuclear inclusions.
